code: hb_blob_create((const char *)data, size, HB_MEMORY_MODE_READONLY, NULL, NULL)
note: Attacker-controlled bytes are wrapped as a font blob, so the input directly drives font parsing and shaping.
The blob is interpreted as a font face, propagating the untrusted bytes into HarfBuzz font tables.
A font object is created from the attacker-controlled face and configured for OpenType shaping.
When the input is large enough, the tail bytes are reinterpreted as UTF-32 codepoints, giving the attacker direct control over shaped text.
The controlled codepoints are loaded into the shaping buffer and become the glyph sequence processed by HarfBuzz.
Shaping dispatches the buffer into the normalization pipeline, which performs decomposition, reordering, and recomposition.

code: buffer->sort (i, end, compare_combining_class); if (plan->shaper->reorder_marks) plan->shaper->reorder_marks (plan, buffer, i, end)
note: Arabic shaping reorders combining marks after sorting them by combining class, creating a mark run that is passed to the complex shaper callback.
The Arabic reordering code merges output clusters before moving marks around, and this is the sink where the MSan report points to use of uninitialized cluster data.
